title: Introduce opaque session proxy and retry-spotlight compiler across SDKs
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: several inconsistencies remain across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs for session lifecycle and retry hint propagation. This has caused subtle resumption bugs during streaming reconnects (notably when a delegated credential path is used) and made it hard for platform teams to reason about retry budgets. This PR introduces an opaque SessionProxy contract (language bindings for Py/TS/Go) plus a small 'retry-spotlight' compiler that turns high-level retry policy hints into per-transport directives. The goal is ergonomics (minimize handshake surface for app devs), parity (same observable behaviour across SDKs), and opt-in stability (no automatic behavioural changes unless caller upgrades).

What I changed (summary):
- Add SessionProxy interface + minimal shim implementations in: sdk-python, sdk-typescript, sdk-go. The proxy centralizes heartbeat/refresh and exposes a single AcquireSession() call that returns an opaque handle.
- Implement retry-spotlight compiler in the TypeScript toolkit and wire a tiny portable JSON output that other SDKs can consume during bootstrap. Compiler maps our retry-dsl (temporal hints, jitter, failover precedence) into transport directives (max-retries, hedging-window-ms, circuit-salvage).
- Python/Go: add lightweight runtime to read the compiler output and apply per-request headers/metadata (no lock-step dependency on TS runtime).
- Tests: unit and integration tests for each SDK demonstrating resume semantics under credential swap and simulated network partial failures.
- Docs: add cross-sdk examples and a migration note in SDK upgrade guide.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked and reviewed (Linear ENG-2149)
- [x] Unit tests for Py/TS/Go
- [x] Integration test using local canary harness (perf-canary repo)
- [x] Add release notes entry
- [x] No breaking changes to public surface without explicit opt-in flags

Related: this ties to earlier work on credential fallback and session-lease (ENG-1991) and the stream-resume investigation from the incident on 2025-11-03.

Notes on compatibility: the SessionProxy is additive and the default SDK factories still return the legacy session behaviour unless callers request the proxy via new factory flag. The retry-spotlight compiler is an opt-in build-time toolchain addition; SDKs that don't consume the JSON output retain current retry behaviour.

If you want to prototype quickly: run packages/sdk-typescript/bin/retry-spotlight --input examples/retry-dsl.yaml --out dist/retry-spotlight.json then set REDWOOD_SESSION_PROXY=1 in the SDK factory environment to consume the spec.
commits: feat(session): add SessionProxy interface to Python SDK and basic shim
feat(ts): implement retry-spotlight compiler + CLI, output portable JSON
feat(go): add session proxy loader and transport-metadata application
test: add unit + integration tests for resume and retry directive application
docs: sdk upgrade guide + quickstart example for session proxy
review_comments: Connor Blake: Overall looks good. Two asks: (1) can the TS compiler emit a minor version field in the JSON so Go/Py can validate compatibility at runtime? (2) tests: add a flakey-network job that toggles token-replacement mid-stream to validate hedging behaviour.

Priya Nair (author): Added a 'spec_version' field to the JSON and implemented a runtime validation check in Go/Python. Added the flakey-network integration test under sdk-typescript/test/integration and wired it into the canary matrix.
Sofia Martinez: Please document the performance implications of reading the compiler JSON on cold start. Suggest lazy-load behind a fast-path check to avoid adding latency to short-lived processes.
Priya Nair (author): Implemented lazy loader with a guarded fast-path (environment variable & factory flag). Updated docs with microbenchmarks (cold start + cached path).
Ethan Liu: nit: rename AcquireSession -> AcquireOpaqueSession to make intent explicit. Also, ensure Acquire returns a context manager / Closeable pattern in Go and Python to avoid leaks.
Priya Nair (author): Renamed to AcquireOpaqueSession and added Close() / __enter__ / __exit__ support. Updated tests accordingly.
merge_outcome: merged on 2026-01-22 via squash with single commit message 'feat: session proxy + retry-spotlight compiler (cross-sdk) - squash'
release_notes: Introduces an opt-in SessionProxy across Python/TypeScript/Go and a TypeScript 'retry-spotlight' compiler that produces a portable retry directive JSON. Opt-in via SDK factory flag. Improves streaming resume semantics and provides a path to unify retry behaviour across languages. No default behaviour changes.
notes_for_backports: Backport only the Python session_proxy shim to the 1.x branch when customers opt-in (requires test matrix). Do not backport the TS compiler.
migration_instructions: 1) Update SDKs to v-next. 2) Generate retry JSON if you want compiled directives. 3) Opt-in by setting REDWOOD_SESSION_PROXY=1 or factory flag session_proxy=true. 4) Validate spec_version in logs.
side_effects: minimal: adds an optional factory flag and a small runtime dependency for JSON parsing in Go/Python. No user-visible changes unless opted in.
qa_notes: Integration test simulates token swap mid-stream and asserts no duplicate commits, hedging triggers within configured window, and session Close() always called. All tests green in CI matrix.
